scope_declines.name: Proposition 2.17 (transpose duality between the inverse Fourier transform and the operator-valued Fourier transform)
scope_declines.reason: Dual-pairing duality of the Fourier transform is C*-algebraic unitary-dual material; no step of this pair uses it.

scope_declines.name: §1.2-1.3 hooks, first-column hook lengths, James's abacus and uniqueness of t-cores
scope_declines.reason: The abacus and t-core material belongs to the later rim-hooks-and-the-murnaghan-nakayama-rule development and is not used by the hook/Rsk pair; only the hook definition and Proposition 1.4(i) are taken from this range (item def-hook-arm-leg-and-hook-length).

scope_declines.name: §9.18 'Yet another version of RSK' (alternate algorithm, stated without proof) and the concluding figure
scope_declines.reason: The alternate algorithm is presented without proof and is not needed by the pair's statements or proofs; the figure is illustrative only.

scope_declines.name: Ch. 3 §3, Exercise 16, p. 118: I(Z,Z)=I(Z×Z,Δ) for half-dimensional Z
scope_declines.reason: This is the self-intersection special case of the diagonal identification; it is the technical core of the intersection-pairings page (DT-12).

scope_declines.name: Corollary 4.2: one-dimensional decomposition into bounded good part and mean-zero bad parts
scope_declines.reason: Same reason as the rising sun lemma: the interval version is superseded by the dyadic ℝ^n decomposition used on this page.

scope_declines.name: Proposition 2.8 (translation covariance of the operator-valued Fourier transform)
scope_declines.reason: This is the operator-field form of translation covariance; the present pair proves only the convolution-operator commutation needed for the spectral argument.

scope_declines.name: Frobenius character formula and the computation of dim V^lambda as a coefficient of the Schur polynomial
scope_declines.reason: The character formula and the identification of V^lambda with the Specht module are the subject of the planned Frobenius-characteristic page; the pair does not use them.

scope_declines.name: Sec. 26.1 and 26.3: characters and the Weyl character formula
scope_declines.reason: The Weyl character formula is commissioned on the later planned page weyl-character-and-multiplicity-formulas (RL-7); the examples here record only the BGG-specific numerical checks.

scope_declines.name: Theorem 3: enumeration of sequences with prescribed longest increasing and decreasing lengths by sums of squares
scope_declines.reason: The enumeration corollary and its Plancherel consequences are owned by the planned Plancherel page; the pair keeps the shape theorem and the sum-of-squares identity only.

scope_declines.name: Ch. 3 §3, p. 116: the Euler characteristic χ(Y)=I(Δ,Δ) of the diagonal
scope_declines.reason: The diagonal self-intersection as the Euler characteristic is the opening construction of the intersection-pairings page (DT-12), which owns the identification.

scope_declines.name: Lemma 4.1: rising sun lemma
scope_declines.reason: A one-dimensional ordered-line precursor; the page needs the dyadic stopping-time decomposition in ℝ^n, which is built instead.

scope_declines.name: Theorem 2.12: Dirichlet partial-sum operators on ℝ and L^p norm convergence
scope_declines.reason: Line Fourier inversion and summation, not singular-integral theory; the page has no claim needing it.

scope_declines.name: Ch. 3 §3, p. 115: odd-dimensional self-intersection vanishes; Möbius nonorientability from I_2(X,X)=1
scope_declines.reason: Self-intersection and its orientability consequences are commissioned for the intersection-pairings page; the factor-interchange sign they use is proved here.

scope_declines.name: §5, pp. 30–31: nonvanishing vector fields on spheres from the antipodal degree
scope_declines.reason: The vector-field application belongs to the Poincare–Hopf page (DT-13); the pair uses only the degree and boundary-sign computations.

scope_declines.name: Definition 2.3 (operator-valued Fourier transform of a measure at an irreducible representation)
scope_declines.reason: The operator-valued Fourier transform and the algebra of operator fields belong to the C*-algebraic unitary-dual development, not to this pair's Hilbert-space Peter-Weyl theorem.

scope_declines.name: §4, pp. 23–25: the mod 2 degree theorem, its homotopy invariance, and examples (constant maps, identity)
scope_declines.reason: The mod 2 degree and the Hopf-type applications are commissioned for the Hopf degree page (DT-18); the count itself is used here only through the parity lemma.

scope_declines.name: Ch. 2 §4, pp. 79–80, Figure 2-15: the Möbius central curve has I_2(X,X)=1 and obstructs orientability
scope_declines.reason: Self-intersection numbers and their Euler-class interpretation are commissioned for the later intersection-pairings page (DT-12); this pair defines the intersection set but does not mint self-intersection or characteristic-class content.

scope_declines.name: Ch. 2 §4, Exercise 14, p. 84: cobordant submanifolds and deformation (the 'trousers' example)
scope_declines.reason: Cobordism of submanifolds and the bordism relation are the commissioned subject of the smooth-cobordism pair (DT-15); the Boundary Theorem needed here is recorded separately.

scope_declines.name: Ch. 3 §3, pp. 110–111: total zero count via the degree of p/|p| and the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
scope_declines.reason: The multiplicity count of polynomial zeros and the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra belong to complex analysis; they are not prerequisites of any item of this pair and are recorded only as the source's application.

scope_declines.name: Proposition 4.7: Whitney decomposition for balls
scope_declines.reason: The ball form of the Whitney cover supports the atomic decomposition on the real Hardy space page, not this page.

scope_declines.name: §7.2 and §7.3 (global differences for noncompact groups; the regular representation as a direct integral (7.4))
scope_declines.reason: Direct integrals, measurable fields and their uniqueness theory are commissioned for the later RG-26 page; the counterexample records only the contrast with the direct-sum definition.

scope_declines.name: §3: BMO as the substitute for L∞, including Proposition 3.4 (CZOs map L∞ to BMO)
scope_declines.reason: The L∞→BMO endpoint is the subject of the later BMO page, which owns its proof in this track.

scope_declines.name: Theorem 2.6 (the Fourier transform is an algebra homomorphism on convolution of measures)
scope_declines.reason: Convolution-algebra duality is commissioned for the C*-algebra page; the present pair uses the Hilbert-space form of Peter-Weyl.

scope_declines.name: Lecture 14, pp. 44–46: Theorems 138/139 (PD[S] is the Thom class of the normal bundle) with the collapse and Poincaré–Lefschetz proof
scope_declines.reason: The identification of the geometric pairing with the Poincare-dual cup pairing is the central theorem of the intersection-pairings page (DT-12); the present pair only fixes the geometric conventions it will consume.

scope_declines.name: §§4.18-4.19 Schur-Weyl duality for gl(V) and GL(V) (Theorems 4.54-4.57 and following)
scope_declines.reason: The complex Schur-Weyl interface is already published on the-branching-rule-and-the-young-graph and is not part of this pair's commissioned claims.

scope_declines.name: Exercise 22 (Fourier analysis on compact abelian groups: characters separate points, uniform density, orthonormal basis)
scope_declines.reason: General compact abelian Fourier theory is commissioned for the LCA dual page; this pair instantiates only the circle, where the published torus items already supply orthonormality and completeness.

scope_declines.name: Exercise 24 (characters separate points of a locally compact abelian group)
scope_declines.reason: Character separation for general abelian groups belongs to the LCA dual page; no general Pontryagin-duality argument is used by this pair.

scope_declines.name: Part II: functorial/categorical BGG resolutions (triangulated and stable infinity-categorical machinery)
scope_declines.reason: Part II uses triangulated and stable infinity-category machinery foreign to this pair's contract and to the design's classical Bruhat-edge proof route; the target theorem is proved in Part I.

scope_declines.name: Lecture 15, p. 50: self-intersection S·S and Theorem 144, the Euler class as the zero locus of a generic section
scope_declines.reason: Self-intersection and the Euler class of the normal bundle are the commissioned core of the intersection-pairings page (DT-12).

scope_declines.name: Exercise 17, Theorem 8 and Exercise 20 (no small subgroups in compact Lie groups; Gleason-Yamabe; inverse limits of linear groups)
scope_declines.reason: The structure theory of general compact groups is not part of this pair's commission; the profinite example uses only the published no-small-subgroups lemma, the published inverse-limit items and the published U(n) Lie-group example.

scope_declines.name: Proposition 4.6: Whitney decomposition with distances comparable to side lengths
scope_declines.reason: The ℝ^n Whitney decomposition is used by the atomic decomposition on the real Hardy space page, where it is planned.

scope_declines.name: Ch. 2 §4, pp. 81–82: one-half Fundamental Theorem of Algebra from deg_2(p/|p|)
scope_declines.reason: The Fundamental Theorem of Algebra and the zero-counting applications are owned by the complex-analysis pages of this library; the pair consumes only the intersection-theoretic mechanism, not this application.

scope_declines.name: §5 dual correspondence: INSERT*, Theorem 1* and the zero-one matrix bijection
scope_declines.reason: Dual (column-insertion) RSK for zero-one matrices is not used by the permutation or two-line-array statements of this pair; only the commutation Lemma 6 of Schensted quotes the dual algorithm.

scope_declines.name: Lemma 7.2 and Theorem 7.3(a): the t-generating-function identity prod(1-t^{h_x})
scope_declines.reason: This t-deformation is used only in Chan's determinant route to the hook formula; the pair proves the formula along the removal-recursion route, so the deformation is not needed and no item is minted for it.

scope_declines.name: Ch. 2 §4, pp. 79–80: the Möbius central curve has I_2(X,X)=1 and thereby obstructs orientability
scope_declines.reason: Self-intersection as a nonorientability obstruction is developed on the intersection-pairings page (DT-12), together with the Euler-class interpretation.

scope_declines.name: Lecture 14, pp. 43–44: Thom class, Euler class and the Poincaré-dual interpretation of a submanifold
scope_declines.reason: Thom and Euler classes as cohomological constructions are owned by the algebraic-topology pages and applied on the intersection-pairings page (DT-12); this pair deliberately mints no characteristic classes.

scope_declines.name: Lemma 5.4.3 (a finite-dimensional subrepresentation of the regular representation consists of continuous functions)
scope_declines.reason: Kowalski needs this lemma only for the alternative route that identifies coefficient spaces with isotypic components of the regular representation; this pair proves uniform density first and derives L^2 completeness from Parseval equivalences, so the lemma is not consumed and is retained as source history.

scope_declines.name: Remark 2.6: the analogous theory on general homogeneous spaces
scope_declines.reason: This page is Euclidean; no general homogeneous-space version is claimed or needed by its consumers.

scope_declines.name: Theorem 5.4.1: uniform Fourier-multiplier bound for doubly truncated kernels and the L² bound 15(A₁+A₂+A₃)
scope_declines.reason: On this page the L² bound of the maximal truncation is obtained inline from Cotlar's inequality and the assumed L² boundedness of T, so no separate local item reproduces this multiplier estimate.

scope_declines.name: Proposition 5.4.9 (Frobenius reciprocity for compact groups)
scope_declines.reason: Induction, rho-functions and Frobenius reciprocity for compact subgroups are commissioned for the later induced-representations page (RG-23); this pair does not consume them.

scope_declines.name: Sec. 30 Chevalley restriction theorem and later sections
scope_declines.reason: These sections concern the Chevalley restriction theorem and geometric representation theory, not the BGG resolution of this pair.

scope_declines.name: Sec. 3 and Sec. 4.3-4.5: sheaf-cohomology applications and algorithm internals
scope_declines.reason: The computational and cohomological applications are outside this pair's contract; only the Sec. 2 structural results about the complex are consumed.

scope_declines.name: Remark 7.1 (Vandermonde determinant and the Young-Frobenius expression for f^lambda)
scope_declines.reason: The Young-Frobenius formula and its character-theoretic proof belong to the planned Frobenius-characteristic page, which is the natural owner of this determinant expression.

scope_declines.name: Sec. 10 Lemma 10.2: nonvanishing of the matrix entries of the strong complex along comparable pairs
scope_declines.reason: Lemma 10.2 is used in Rocha-Caridi to normalise signs through the real form; this page obtains the compatible signs by the recorded two-route proof of the sign lemma and does not need the full nonvanishing statement.

scope_declines.name: Proposition 4.5: dyadic Whitney decomposition
scope_declines.reason: Whitney decompositions belong to the stopping-time machinery of the real Hardy space page, not to the singular-integral page.

scope_declines.name: §5, pp. 30–31: examples z↦z^k and the antipodal map; nonvanishing vector fields on spheres
scope_declines.reason: The vector-field application and the antipodal degree computation belong to the Poincare–Hopf page (DT-13) and the Hopf degree page respectively; they are not prerequisites of this pair.

scope_declines.name: Problem 4.4: conditional-expectation interpretation of the good part
scope_declines.reason: An exercise recording an interpretation only; the page needs the quantitative decomposition bounds, which are built as items.

scope_declines.name: Ch. 2 §4, pp. 80–81: mod 2 degree deg_2(f)=I_2(f,{y}) and its constancy; homotopy invariance
scope_declines.reason: The mod 2 degree as an invariant and its sphere applications are the commissioned subject of the Hopf degree page (DT-18); this pair only recovers the integral degree sign formula on its B page.

scope_declines.name: Theorem 9.3: the splitting theorem (weak resolution terms split into generalized Vermas)
scope_declines.reason: Rocha-Caridi's splitting theorem is her alternative route to the strong resolution; this page instead proves exactness directly by the n-minus-coinvariant argument of BGG, so the Ext and projective machinery of Secs. 3-9 is not rebuilt here.

scope_declines.name: §6 Theorems 5-6 (plactic equivalence and the invariance of the P-tableau)
scope_declines.reason: The plactic monoid and the elementary-transformation characterization are not needed for the hook formula, the RSK bijection or the subsequence theorem; the pair records them here as declined source content.

scope_declines.name: Theorem 4: symmetric matrices correspond to tableaux and odd-length columns to the trace
scope_declines.reason: The symmetric-matrix specialization and its odd-column trace statistic are not among the pair's commissioned claims; the P=Q principle used for involutions is taken from the permutation specialization instead.

scope_declines.name: Sec. 3.3 Weyl character formula in final form (Theorem Weyl Character)
scope_declines.reason: The formula itself is commissioned on the later planned page weyl-character-and-multiplicity-formulas (RL-7); this page scaffolds only the BGG Euler-character/numerator identity RL-7 consumes.

scope_declines.name: Formula (5): dim V^lambda = (n!/prod_j l_j!)·det(l_j^{N-i}) = (n!/prod l_j!)·prod_{i<j}(l_i-l_j) via Vandermonde
scope_declines.reason: The determinant reduction is the analytic skeleton of Etingof's route and requires the Frobenius character formula; the pair proves the same dimension by the removable-node recursion, so this intermediate formula is not built.
